aciklama: Gaziantep's legendary breakfast soup — shredded lamb, rice, garlic, and red pepper butter in a rich bone broth. Traditionally eaten at dawn.
A festive Gaziantep dish featuring tiny, hand-rolled rice and meat dumplings with chickpeas, simmered in a creamy warm yogurt broth and drizzled with mint oil.
Tangy meatball soup sharpened with pomegranate molasses and lemon — a delicate balance of sour and savory.
Hand-minced lamb and tail fat seasoned simply with salt and red capsicum peppers, grilled over charcoal and served on flatbread.
Fire-roasted eggplant blended with garlic yogurt, crowned with sautéed spiced lamb chunks. A dish fit for a sultan.
A unique Gaziantep kebab where minced lamb is kneaded with fine bulgur wheat (locally called 'simit'), fresh mint, and spices, then grilled on skewers.
Small cubes of lamb liver and tail fat seasoned with cumin and chili, quickly grilled on skewers and wrapped in thin lavaş flatbread.
Alternating pieces of sliced eggplant and hand-minced lamb meatballs threaded on a skewer and charred over open coals.
Gaziantep’s most prized meat delicacy — exceptionally tender lamb tenderloin, lightly seasoned and quickly grilled over charcoal to melt-in-your-mouth perfection.
Crispy bulgur shell stuffed with spiced ground meat, pine nuts and walnuts — either fried or boiled in broth.
Paper-thin dough spread with a mixture of minced lamb, garlic, tomatoes, and herbs (no onion), baked in a stone oven.
Gossamer-thin dough layers folded over clotted cream (kaymak) and crushed pistachios, baked until crispy. Antep's most beloved breakfast sweet.
Wafer-thin pastry sheets hand-rolled around a filling of ground pistachio and sugar, soaked in light syrup.
Pilaf made from fire-dried green wheat (firik) with lamb, giving a distinctive smoky, nutty aroma. A Gaziantep staple.
Sun-dried vegetables (eggplant and pepper) hollowed and filled with a spiced rice-and-lamb mixture, simmered in a tangy sumac and tomato broth.
A popular Gaziantep street food featuring tender, spiced boiled chickpeas wrapped in warm flatbread with fresh onions, parsley, and lemon.
A traditional Gaziantep stew made with tender lamb, fresh green garlic, leeks, and chickpeas in a rich, tangy yogurt sauce.
Dozens of hand-stretched phyllo layers, brushed with clarified butter, packed with fresh Antep pistachios and drenched in light syrup. The world standard.
Shredded wheat (kadayıf) sandwiching unsalted white cheese, baked in clarified butter until golden, soaked in syrup and topped with crushed pistachio.
Phyllo pastry triangles filled with a rich milk-and-semolina cream (or kaymak) and pistachios, baked to golden perfection and soaked in sweet syrup.
Whole walnuts threaded on string, dipped repeatedly in thickened grape must until they form a firm, chewy molasses log.
